located within the Los Angeles, California fashion district (referred to hereafter as the
“Los Angeles Fashion District GTO”).12 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO applied
to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

course of its trade or business, received currency in excess of $3,000 in one transaction
or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

behavioral.summary: The account of SYN_cd180308, a low-risk grocery store business, shows a total of 7 transactions amounting to $1,139,445.98. Activity is concentrated in cash channels, with a channel mix of 0.714 for cash, 0.143 for ach, and 0.143 for wire. The highest single transaction was $346,028.23 via wire on 2026-04-19. The entity exhibited a velocity of 3 transactions in 24 hours on 2026-02-11. The observed volume is 2.68 times the declared monthly volume of $424,468.00. Notable cash activity includes deposits from Daniel Moore ($103,127.53), Sarah Jackson ($272,691.05), and Patricia Brown ($347,101.88).

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Yes, the conduct described falls within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 because the entity conducted multiple cash deposits (e.g., $103,127.53 on 2026-03-17 and $272,691.05 on 2026-03-18) that appear designed to evade the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5322.
statutory.label: entailment
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring transactions to evade the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5322. The fact pattern describes a business with a multi-shift cash operation that conducted several large cash deposits (including $103,127.53 and $272,691.05) which, if done to avoid triggering a Currency Transaction Report (CTR), would constitute structuring under § 5324.
